issues.description: Method messageOnMilk: the problem statement's Part 2 (lines 92-95 in problem_statement.md) explicitly describes messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) that returns a string including the milkVolume, but the UML in the same problem statement (lines 51-53) and all provided code use a no-argument signature messageOnMilk(): String. The template's example usage (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, commented lines 30-32) calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments, and the solution defines the interface and implementations as messageOnMilk() with no parameters (solution Milkable.java signature at line 5; Seal.java implements messageOnMilk() at line 19; Goat.java implements messageOnMilk() at line 15). This contradiction between the textual requirement (double parameter) and the UML/code (no parameter) will confuse students about which method signature to implement and can lead to compilation or test failures if they follow the wrong variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and the code. Recommended: update the problem statement Part 2 text to refer to messageOnMilk() with no parameters and show the expected return format (e.g., "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), matching the UML, template, and solution. If milk volume must be included, instead update the UML, the Milkable interface, the template usage, and all implementations to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update tests/examples accordingly.
